title: Daily life
goal: Describe your daily routine, say how often you do things and in what order, and talk about places and getting around.

notes.p: Most routine words are a verb plus an object: {{起身|hei2 san1}} get up, {{沖涼|cung1 loeng4}} shower, {{返工|faan1 gung1}} go to work, {{放工|fong3 gung1}} get off work, {{瞓覺|fan3 gaau3}} sleep. Meals: {{食早餐|sik6 zou2 caan1}} breakfast, {{食晏|sik6 aan3}} lunch, {{食晚飯|sik6 maan5 faan6}} dinner. The time goes BEFORE the verb: {{我七點起身|ngo5 cat1 dim2 hei2 san1}}. Sound trap: {{瞓|fan3}} sleep has a short vowel; {{飯|faan6}} rice has a long 'aa' and a low tone.
ex: ngo5 ping4 si4 je6 maan5 cung1 loeng4
nei5 gei2 dim2 fong3 gung1 aa3
What time do you get off work?

notes.p: Frequency words go after the person and before the verb: {{每日|mui5 jat6}} every day, {{成日|seng4 jat6}} often, {{有時|jau5 si4}} sometimes, {{間中|gaan3 zung1}} now and then, {{好少|hou2 siu2}} rarely. With {{每日|mui5 jat6}} people often add {{都|dou1}}: {{我每日都飲咖啡|ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 jam2 gaa3 fe1}}. 'Never' as a habit is {{從來唔|cung4 loi4 m4}} + verb. Counting times uses {{次|ci3}} with {{兩|loeng5}}, not {{二|ji6}}: {{一個禮拜兩次|jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 loeng5 ci3}}. Note {{成日|seng4 jat6}} is said seng4, not sing4.
ex: ngo5 seng4 jat6 daap3 dei6 tit3
ngo5 cung4 loi4 m4 jam2 gaa3 fe1
ngo5 jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 heoi3 loeng5 ci3

notes.p: {{先|sin1}} goes before the first action and {{然後|jin4 hau6}} before the next: {{我先沖涼，然後食早餐|ngo5 sin1 cung1 loeng4, jin4 hau6 sik6 zou2 caan1}}. 'As soon as A, B' is {{一|jat1}} + A + {{就|zau6}} + B. {{完|jyun4}} after a verb means 'finish': {{食完飯之後|sik6 jyun4 faan6 zi1 hau6}} after eating.
ex: ngo5 jat1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 zau6 zyu2 faan6
As soon as I get home, I cook.
sik6 jyun4 faan6 zi1 hau6, ngo5 sai2 saam1
After eating, I do the laundry.

notes.p: {{搭|daap3}} = ride, take: {{搭巴士|daap3 baa1 si2}}, {{搭地鐵|daap3 dei6 tit3}}, {{搭的士|daap3 dik1 si2}}. {{揸車|zaa1 ce1}} = drive (you hold the wheel). {{行路|haang4 lou6}} = walk. How you go comes before where you go: {{我搭地鐵返工|ngo5 daap3 dei6 tit3 faan1 gung1}}. Ask with {{點樣|dim2 joeng2}}. On a minibus, call out {{有落！|jau5 lok6}} to get off. {{巴士|baa1 si2}} ends with a rising tone, like {{的士|dik1 si2}}.
ex: nei5 dim2 joeng2 faan1 gung1 aa3
How do you get to work?

notes.p: 'At' a place is {{喺|hai2}} (rising), not {{係|hai6}} (low) 'to be': {{喺屋企|hai2 uk1 kei2}}, {{喺公司|hai2 gung1 si1}}. Fresh food comes from the {{街市|gaai1 si5}} wet market; packaged things from the {{超級市場|ciu1 kap1 si5 coeng4}}. {{買餸|maai5 sung3}} = buy food for meals. In {{廚房|cyu4 fong2}} and {{公園|gung1 jyun2}} the last syllable rises.
ex: 今晚你喺唔喺屋企食飯呀？
gam1 maan5 nei5 hai2 m4 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6 aa3
Are you eating at home tonight?
ngo5 gaan3 zung1 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai5 sung3
Now and then I go to the wet market for groceries.

vocab.note: The everyday word for showering or bathing.
{{晏|aan3}} = late in the day; this is the everyday word for lunch.
Literally 'cook rice', but used for cooking a meal.

vocab.en: to finish work for the day

t: nei5 gei2 dim2 fong3 gung1 aa3
vocab.en: What time do you get off work?

vocab.note: A caring thing to say. {{瞓|fan3}} = sleep.

t: ngo5 cung4 loi4 m4 jam2 gaa3 fe1
nei5 ping4 si4 gei2 dim2 hei2 san1 aa3
vocab.en: What time do you usually get up?

t: jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 loeng5 ci3

vocab.note: {{二十分鐘|ji6 sap6 fan1 zung1}} = twenty minutes.

t: ngo5 sin1 cung1 loeng4, jin4 hau6 sik6 zou2 caan1
vocab.en: I shower first, then have breakfast

t: ngo5 jat1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 zau6 cung1 loeng4
vocab.en: As soon as I get home, I shower

t: nei5 dim2 joeng2 faan1 gung1 aa3
vocab.en: How do you get to work?

vocab.note: Minibus drivers stop when you call this out.

q: ngo5 mui5 jat6 cat1 dim2 ___ san1
items.en: I get up at seven every day.
items.why: {{起身|hei2 san1}} = get up.

q: ngo5 ping4 si4 je6 maan5 ___ loeng4
items.en: I usually shower at night.
items.why: {{沖涼|cung1 loeng4}} is the everyday word for showering.

q: ngo5 ___ daap3 dei6 tit3 faan1 gung1
items.en: I often take the MTR to work.
items.why: {{成日|seng4 jat6}} = often. {{好少|hou2 siu2}} = rarely; {{有時|jau5 si4}} = sometimes.

items.en: I rarely drive.
items.why: {{揸車|zaa1 ce1}} = drive.

q: ngo5 sin1 sik6 zou2 caan1, ___ faan1 gung1
items.en: I have breakfast first, then go to work.
items.why: {{先|sin1}} … {{然後|jin4 hau6}} … = first …, then ….

q: ngo5 jat1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 ___ cung1 loeng4
items.en: As soon as I get home, I shower.
items.why: {{一|jat1}} + A + {{就|zau6}} + B = as soon as A, B. The {{一|jat1}} needs {{就|zau6}}.

items.en: How do you get to work?
items.why: {{點樣|dim2 joeng2}} = how, in what way.

items.en: I take the bus to work.
items.why: {{搭|daap3}} = ride, take (a bus, the MTR, a taxi).

q: ngo5 gaan3 zung1 heoi3 ___ maai5 sung3
items.en: Now and then I go to the wet market for groceries.
items.why: {{街市|gaai1 si5}} = wet market.

q: ngo5 jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 heoi3 loeng5 ___
items.en: I go twice a week.
items.why: {{次|ci3}} counts how many times: {{兩次|loeng5 ci3}} = twice.

q: 食完飯___，我哋去公園行吓啦
sik6 jyun4 faan6 ___, ngo5 dei6 heoi3 gung1 jyun2 haang4 haa5 laa1
items.en: After eating, let's go for a walk in the park.
items.why: {{食完飯之後|sik6 jyun4 faan6 zi1 hau6}} = after eating. 'Finished eating' and 'before' don't go together.

q: ngo5 hou2 je6 ___, so2 ji5 ziu1 zou2 hou2 gui6
items.en: I go to bed late, so I'm tired in the morning.
items.why: {{瞓|fan3}} = sleep: mid level tone, short vowel. {{飯|faan6}} is rice, {{粉|fan2}} rice noodles.

items.en: I never drink coffee.
items.why: {{從來唔|cung4 loi4 m4}} + verb = never, as a habit.

q: gam1 maan5 nei5 hai2 ___ uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6 aa3
items.en: Are you eating at home tonight?
items.why: A-not-A with {{喺|hai2}} 'be at': {{喺唔喺|hai2 m4 hai2}}. {{係|hai6}} 'to be' is the low-tone look-alike.

q: nei5 ping4 si4 gei2 dim2 fong3 gung1 ___
items.en: What time do you usually get off work?
items.why: {{呀|aa3}} softens a question. A final {{咩|me1}} is only for surprised yes/no questions, {{未|mei6}} asks 'yet?', and {{咗|zo2}} can't describe a habit.

q: ngo5 ___ cung1 loeng4, jin4 hau6 sik6 zou2 caan1
items.en: I shower first, then have breakfast.
items.why: {{先|sin1}} before the first action, {{然後|jin4 hau6}} before the next.

items.q: A colleague asks when you get off work. You finish at six. You say:
items.why: {{六點|luk6 dim2}} = six o'clock; {{六號|luk6 hou6}} is the 6th of the month.

items.q: You're on a Hong Kong minibus and want the driver to stop at the next corner. You call out:
items.why: {{有落！|jau5 lok6}} tells the minibus driver someone is getting off.

items.q: A friend asks how you get to work. You go on foot. You say:
opts: ngo5 daap3 baa1 si2 faan1 gung1
items.why: How you go comes first: {{行路|haang4 lou6}}, then {{返工|faan1 gung1}}.

items.q: You want to say that you hardly ever cook. You say:
opts: ngo5 hou2 zung1 ji3 zyu2 faan6
items.why: {{好少|hou2 siu2}} = rarely.

items.q: It's 1 a.m. and your partner is still up working. You gently tell them to get some sleep:
items.why: {{早啲瞓啦|zou2 di1 fan3 laa1}} 'go to bed earlier' is what Hong Kongers say, even late at night. {{啦|laa1}} makes it a gentle nudge.

items.q: Someone asks what you do on Sundays. You go to the park now and then. You say:
opts: ngo5 gaan3 zung1 heoi3 gung1 jyun2
ngo5 cung4 loi4 m4 heoi3 gung1 jyun2
ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 gung1 jyun2
items.why: {{間中|gaan3 zung1}} = now and then, a habit. {{去咗|heoi3 zo2}} is one past trip.

items.q: You're running late because of traffic. You message your friend:
opts: 唔好意思，塞車，我遲啲到
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, sak1 ce1, ngo5 ci4 di1 dou3
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 zaa1 gan2 baa1 si2
mou5 man6 tai4, ngo5 zou2 dou3 zo2
items.why: Apologise, give the reason ({{塞車|sak1 ce1}}), and say you'll be late: {{遲啲到|ci4 di1 dou3}}.

items.q: Your friend asks where you're having dinner tonight. You're eating at home. You say:
items.why: 'At' is {{喺|hai2}}, rising. {{係|hai6}} (low) means 'to be'.

opts: I go to bed at seven.
I get off work at seven.
items.why: {{七|cat1}} seven ({{一|jat1}} is one); {{起身|hei2 san1}} get up.

say: ngo5 seng4 jat6 daap3 baa1 si2
items.why: {{成日|seng4 jat6}} = often; {{搭巴士|daap3 baa1 si2}} = take the bus.
{{好少|hou2 siu2}} = rarely; {{煮飯|zyu2 faan6}} = cook, not {{食飯|sik6 faan6}} eat.

say: ngo5 jat1 fong3 gung1 zau6 faan1 uk1 kei2
opts: As soon as I get off work, I go home.
As soon as I get home, I go to work.
I don't go home after work.
He goes home as soon as he gets off work.
As soon as I get off work, I go to the market.
I get off work at one and go home.
items.why: {{一|jat1}} … {{就|zau6}} … = as soon as. One o'clock would be {{一點|jat1 dim2}}.

say: ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 aan3
opts: I have lunch at the office.
items.why: {{喺屋企|hai2 uk1 kei2}} = at home; {{食晏|sik6 aan3}} = have lunch.

say: jat1 go3 lai5 baai3 loeng5 ci3
items.why: {{兩次|loeng5 ci3}} = two times; {{一個禮拜|jat1 go3 lai5 baai3}} = in a week.

say: nei5 ping4 si4 dim2 joeng2 faan1 hok6 aa3
opts: How do you usually get to school?
When do you usually go to school?
How do you usually get to work?
Do you usually walk to school?
items.why: {{點樣|dim2 joeng2}} = how; {{返學|faan1 hok6}} = go to school ({{返工|faan1 gung1}} is work).

say: ngo5 gaan3 zung1 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai5 sung3
opts: Now and then I go to the wet market for groceries.
I often go to the wet market for groceries.
I never go to the wet market.
Now and then I go to the supermarket for groceries.
Now and then I sell food at the wet market.
I'm at the wet market buying groceries.
items.why: {{間中|gaan3 zung1}} = now and then. {{買|maai5}} buy rises; {{賣|maai6}} sell is low.

opts: The bus is really cheap today.
items.why: {{塞車|sak1 ce1}} = traffic jam; {{好|hou2}} = very.
{{瞓|fan3}} = sleep; {{早啲|zou2 di1}} = earlier. 'Good night' is {{早唞|zou2 tau2}}.

s: 你平時幾點起身呀？
nei5 ping4 si4 gei2 dim2 hei2 san1 aa3
turns.en: What time do you usually get up?

opts: ngo5 ping4 si4 cat1 dim2 hei2 san1
ngo5 ping4 si4 cat1 dim2 fan3 gaau3
ngo5 ping4 si4 cat1 hou6 hei2 san1
turns.why: {{七點|cat1 dim2}} = seven o'clock; {{起身|hei2 san1}} = get up.

s: 好早呀！你點樣返工呀？
hou2 zou2 aa3! nei5 dim2 joeng2 faan1 gung1 aa3
turns.en: That's early! How do you get to work?

opts: ngo5 daap3 dei6 tit3 faan1 gung1
ngo5 zaa1 dei6 tit3 faan1 gung1
ngo5 haang4 dei6 tit3 faan1 gung1
turns.why: Passengers {{搭|daap3}} the MTR. {{揸|zaa1}} is for driving.

s: 要幾耐呀？
jiu3 gei2 noi6 aa3

turns.why: A length of time in minutes: {{分鐘|fan1 zung1}}. {{點|dim2}} is a clock time, {{號|hou6}} a date.

s: 今晚你喺唔喺屋企食飯呀？
gam1 maan5 nei5 hai2 m4 hai2 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6 aa3
turns.en: Are you eating at home tonight?

s: 好呀！今晚邊個煮飯呀？
hou2 aa3! gam1 maan5 bin1 go3 zyu2 faan6 aa3

opts: 我煮啦，我一放工就去街市買餸
ngo5 zyu2 laa1, ngo5 jat1 fong3 gung1 zau6 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai5 sung3
我煮啦，我一放工就去街市賣餸
ngo5 zyu2 laa1, ngo5 jat1 fong3 gung1 zau6 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai6 sung3
我煮咗喇，我一放工就去街市買餸
ngo5 zyu2 zo2 laa3, ngo5 jat1 fong3 gung1 zau6 heoi3 gaai1 si5 maai5 sung3
turns.why: {{買餸|maai5 sung3}} = buy groceries ({{賣|maai6}} would be 'sell'). You haven't cooked yet, so no {{咗|zo2}}.

s: 唔該晒！我買啤酒啦
m4 goi1 saai3! ngo5 maai5 be1 zau2 laa1
turns.en: Thanks so much! I'll buy the beer.

s: 你每日都飲咖啡呀？
nei5 mui5 jat6 dou1 jam2 gaa3 fe1 aa3
turns.en: Do you drink coffee every day?

opts: m4 hai6, ngo5 jau5 si4 jam2
m4 hai6, ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 jam2
turns.why: 'No, just sometimes': {{有時|jau5 si4}}. Saying {{每日都飲|mui5 jat6 dou1 jam2}} after 'no' contradicts yourself.

s: 我從來唔飲咖啡，我飲茶
ngo5 cung4 loi4 m4 jam2 gaa3 fe1, ngo5 jam2 caa4
turns.en: I never drink coffee. I drink tea.

opts: 真係？你每日飲幾多杯呀？
zan1 hai6? nei5 mui5 jat6 jam2 gei2 do1 bui1 aa3
真係？你每日飲幾多碗呀？
zan1 hai6? nei5 mui5 jat6 jam2 gei2 do1 wun2 aa3
真係？你每日飲幾多位呀？
zan1 hai6? nei5 mui5 jat6 jam2 gei2 do1 wai2 aa3
turns.why: Drinks are counted in cups: {{杯|bui1}}. {{碗|wun2}} is a bowl; {{位|wai2}} counts people.

s: 三杯！朝早一杯，晏晝兩杯
saam1 bui1! ziu1 zou2 jat1 bui1, aan3 zau3 loeng5 bui1
turns.en: Three! One in the morning and two in the afternoon.

s: 早晨！你去邊度呀？
zou2 san4! nei5 heoi3 bin1 dou6 aa3
turns.en: Morning! Where are you off to?

opts: ngo5 heoi3 ciu1 kap1 si5 coeng4
ngo5 hai2 ciu1 kap1 si5 coeng4
ngo5 hai6 ciu1 kap1 si5 coeng4
turns.why: She asked where you're going: {{去|heoi3}}. {{喺|hai2}} = be at; {{係|hai6}} = to be.

s: 你行路去呀？好遠㗎！
nei5 haang4 lou6 heoi3 aa3? hou2 jyun5 gaa3
turns.en: Are you walking there? It's really far!

opts: m4 hai6, ngo5 daap3 baa1 si2
m4 hai6, ngo5 zaa1 baa1 si2
hai6, ngo5 daap3 zo2 baa1 si2
turns.why: Passengers {{搭|daap3}} the bus. The third answer says 'yes, walking' and 'took the bus' at once.

s: 巴士站喺嗰度，一直行就到
baa1 si2 zaam6 hai2 go2 dou6, jat1 zik6 haang4 zau6 dou3
turns.en: The bus stop is over there. Go straight and you're there.

turns.why: She helped you: {{唔該晒|m4 goi1 saai3}}. {{早唞|zou2 tau2}} is 'good night'.

s: 你禮拜日平時做咩呀？
nei5 lai5 baai3 jat6 ping4 si4 zou6 me1 aa3
turns.en: What do you usually do on Sundays?

opts: ngo5 sin1 zap1 uk1, jin4 hau6 heoi3 gung1 jyun2
ngo5 jin4 hau6 zap1 uk1, sin1 heoi3 gung1 jyun2
ngo5 sin1 zap1 uk1, zi1 cin4 heoi3 gung1 jyun2
turns.why: {{先|sin1}} comes with the first action, {{然後|jin4 hau6}} with the second.

s: 你成日去公園㗎？
nei5 seng4 jat6 heoi3 gung1 jyun2 gaa3
turns.en: You go to the park a lot?

opts: hai6 aa3, mui5 go3 lai5 baai3 jat6 dou1 heoi3
hai6 aa3, ngo5 hou2 siu2 heoi3
係呀，每個禮拜日都去咗
hai6 aa3, mui5 go3 lai5 baai3 jat6 dou1 heoi3 zo2
turns.why: {{每個禮拜日都去|mui5 go3 lai5 baai3 jat6 dou1 heoi3}} = I go every Sunday. A habit takes no {{咗|zo2}}, and 'yes' + 'rarely' contradicts.

s: 好呀，下次我同你一齊去！
hou2 aa3, haa6 ci3 ngo5 tung4 nei5 jat1 cai4 heoi3
turns.en: Nice, next time I'll go with you!

roleplay.title: Comparing daily routines
roleplay.setup: You're chatting with Wing, a Hong Kong office worker, about a normal weekday. Swap routines: when you get up, how you get to work, and what you do in the evening.
roleplay.persona: You are Wing, a friendly Hong Kong office worker in your late twenties. Your weekday: you get up at seven, shower, have breakfast at a cha chaan teng, take the MTR to work in Central (about thirty minutes), get off work around seven in the evening, rarely cook, often eat dinner with friends, and go to bed late, around one o'clock. Ask the learner about their routine one question at a time and react naturally, sharing your own. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1-8: routine verbs, how-often words (every day, often, sometimes, now and then, rarely), first-then, as-soon-as, and transport. If the learner struggles, rephrase more simply.
opening: nei5 ping4 si4 gei2 dim2 hei2 san1 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: What time do you usually get up?
goals: Say how you get to work

roleplay.title: Chatting with a neighbour
roleplay.setup: You meet Auntie Wong, your neighbour, outside your building in the morning. Tell her where you're going and how, and ask her about the local wet market.
roleplay.persona: You are Auntie Wong, a chatty retired Hong Kong woman in your sixties who lives next door. You go to the wet market almost every morning because the food is fresher than at the supermarket; it is a ten-minute walk, or two stops by bus. You cook every day for your family. Ask the learner where they are going and how they are getting there, recommend the wet market, and ask whether they cook at home. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, mostly with words from levels 1-8. Be warm and a little nosy; rephrase simply if the learner is stuck.
opening: zou2 san4! heoi3 bin1 dou6 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: Morning! Where are you off to?
goals: Say how you are getting there
Ask how often she goes to the wet market
Say whether you cook at home
